title: Anisotropic noise contraction
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $r_i\in\mathbb R$ be a rate for each coordinate, and let $T_{\boldsymbol r}$ denote the anisotropic noise operator and $N_{i,r_i}$ the noise operator on coordinate $i$. If $\|N_{i,r_i}g\|_{q,P}\leq\|g\|_{q,P}$ for every coordinate $i$ and every real-valued function $g$ on the product, then $\|T_{\boldsymbol r}f\|_{q,P}\leq\|f\|_{q,P}$ for every real-valued function $f$ on the product.
hypotheses_covered: A product of n finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and coordinate weights summing to one
A real rate r_i for each coordinate i
For every coordinate i and real-valued function g, the coordinate noise operator N_{i,r_i} does not increase the real moment norm
Real-valued function f on the product
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $q\in\mathbb R$, and rates $r_i\in\mathbb R$. If $\|N_{i,r_i}g\|_{q,P}\le\|g\|_{q,P}$ for every coordinate $i$ and every real $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, then $\|T_{\boldsymbol r}f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{q,P}$ for every real $f$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_{\boldsymbol s}h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(\prod_{i\in S}s_i)h_S$ for real coordinate rates $s_i$; $N_{i,a}h=E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h+a(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)$; $\|h\|_{q,P}:=(\mathbb E_P|h|^q)^{1/q}$ as a totalized moment expression for every real $q$, with $1/0=0$, $0^0=1$, and $0^b=0$ for $b\ne0$.
